outlook.statement: India's outlook for CY 2026 remains encouraging with GDP growth projected at 6.9%, supported by improved rural liquidity, stable urban demand, and RBI's calibrated rate cuts, presenting significant opportunity for responsible credit expansion in MSME and retail segments.

NBFC sectoral AUM expected to surpass ₹60 Trillion in FY 2025–26, with the sector expanding in reach and responsibility, pivoting towards secured, granular portfolios and sustainable balance sheet structures.

Company intends to continue efforts of mainstreaming financial inclusion and providing affordable credit, expanding operations in existing areas, expanding to newer geographies through organic and inorganic opportunities.

India's potential growth rate is estimated at around 7%, reaffirming the country's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year. NBFCs will continue to grow in the financial ecosystem and create meaningful financial inclusion, furthering the Government's agenda of Make in India and Start-Up India.
Some of the opportunities for the business of your Company include demographic changes and an under-penetrated market, use of digital solutions for business/collections, and economic upliftment.

Interest Rate Risk: The risk arising from a financial loss, owing to unfavourable interest rates for both lending and treasury operations.
Credit Risk: The risk arising from the potential loss due to borrowers and/or counterparties failing to fulfil their contractual obligations.
Operational Risk: Risk about failure of processes and controls in operations, which can also have an adverse impact on business continuity, reputation and profitability.
Regulatory Risk: Any non-compliance with regulations could result in monetary losses and has the capability to damage the Company's reputation.
Fraud Risk: Loan fraud, identity theft, internal fraud, and cyber fraud posing threat of financial loss and reputation loss.
Liquidity Risk: The risk arises when the Company is unable to fulfil its financial obligations as required or within predetermined timelines.
Cash Management Risk: Possible obstacles and risks encountered in the collection of loan instalments, pertaining to ensuring timely and complete receipt of payments from borrowers.
Information Technology Risk: Risk stemming from IT infrastructure failure or threats to data integrity, leading to operational disruptions and financial losses.
Cybersecurity Risk: Risk stemming from cyberattacks and hacking due to heightened reliance on the internet and digital platforms.
Slow industrial growth, stiff competition within the NBFC and banking sectors, entry of many banking and non-banking companies.

The Company has complied with the mandatory requirements as stipulated under the SEBI Regulations as and when applicable from time to time.

The Company has implemented 'Whistle Blower Policy' covering Vigil Mechanism with protective clauses for the Whistle Blowers. During the financial year ended March 31, 2026, no Whistle Blower complaints were received from the employees and Directors of the Company.
